name: London Lowball
description: London Lowball is a specific variant of Seven Card Stud played for the 'Low' hand, essentially similar to Razz but traditionally played in London card rooms with Pot-Limit or Spread-Limit structures. The goal is to make the worst possible five-card poker hand out of seven cards dealt. In London rules, the Ace is always low, and straights and flushes do not count against the player, making A-2-3-4-5 the 'nuts' (best possible hand).

content.text: London Lowball is a specific variant of Seven Card Stud played for the 'Low' hand, essentially similar to Razz but traditionally played in London card rooms with Pot-Limit or Spread-Limit structures. The goal is to make the worst possible five-card poker hand out of seven cards dealt. In London rules, the Ace is always low, and straights and flushes do not count against the player, making A-2-3-4-5 the 'nuts' (best possible hand).
Developed in the 1970s and 80s in London gaming clubs like the Victoria Casino ('The Vic'). It adapted American Razz rules to the British preference for Pot-Limit betting.
Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.
Two cards face-down, one card face-up to begin. Subsequent rounds follow the 7-card stud pattern (4th, 5th, 6th streets up, 7th street down).

items.text: 2-7 Triple Draw: A draw-poker version where straights/flushes DO count.
Stud Hi-Lo: Split pot between high and low hands.
